plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for Alpine Optoelectronics TDCM-EDFA optical transmission chassis. It reports uptime, per-fan speed and state, PSU input/output state, output voltage, slot temperature and EDFA temperature, based on the ALPINE-TDCM-EDFA-MIB (enterprise PEN 52326). There is no host CPU% or memory%.
name: Transmission

metrics.name: device_fan_speed
metrics.description: Fan rotation speed in RPM of each Alpine TDCM-EDFA system fan (alpineTEFanCardFan1/2/3Speed). Fans numbered above FansTotalCnt are dropped. Negative values and readings above 30000 RPM are dropped.

metrics.name: device_fan_state
metrics.description: Operational state of each Alpine TDCM-EDFA system fan (alpineTEFanCardFan1/2/3Status), normalised to 1=normal / 2=abnormal. Unknown codes are dropped.

metrics.name: device_psu_input_state
metrics.description: PSU input state of the Alpine TDCM-EDFA power card (alpineTEPowerCardPowerInStatus): On→1 (normal), Off→2 (abnormal). Other codes are dropped.

metrics.name: device_psu_output_state
metrics.description: PSU output state of the Alpine TDCM-EDFA power card (alpineTEPowerCardPowerOutStatus): Normal→1, Voltage High/Low→2 (abnormal). Other codes are dropped.

metrics.name: device_voltage_volts
metrics.description: PSU output voltage of the Alpine TDCM-EDFA power card in volts (alpineTEPowerCardPowerOutVal OCTET STRING). Unparsable or non-positive values are dropped.

metrics.name: slot_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: Slot temperature of the Alpine TDCM-EDFA chassis in degrees Celsius (alpineTEBISlotTemperature). The device reports an OCTET STRING; unparsable values and readings outside -40..125 C are dropped.

metrics.name: edfa_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: EDFA module temperature in degrees Celsius (gceTemperature). The device reports an OCTET STRING; unparsable values and readings outside -40..125 C are dropped. Kept distinct from slot_temperature_celsius so the two tables never share a series.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
